acceptanceCriteria: `make dogfood-change` accepts a per-hunk citation plan (or derives one from the change's affected-plan evidence) and refuses a plan that cites one span for every hunk of a non-chore change, with the refusal reason naming the hunk count and the single span.

The chore bind/seal maps carry an explicit producer-written marker (a `kind` or `role` member admitted by the V1-1265 stable schema's producer-only-members list) and `corvint cem status --citation` reports them under a separate class in the summary, so decision 0525's migration baseline (V1-1277) can compare like with like.

A rerun of the 593-map baseline script over the first 30 post-cutover dogfood maps shows invariant <= 10% and specificity > 0 for every non-chore map, retained as a build-log entry; a worse result is retained as a failed evaluation, not hidden.
docs/DOGFOOD.md documents the per-hunk plan shape and the chore-map class; V1-1276 cites this ticket before its cutover lands.
body: Source: decision 0523 P0 baseline over the 593 committed cem/0.2 maps at origin/main f0d0e6106 (docs/build-log/2026-10-12-cem-citation-baseline-593-maps.md, evidence under docs/build-log/evidence/v1-1262/). Observed: 180 of 592 citation blocks are invariant (every hunk cites the same evidence set); 171 of those are the `chore: bind change evidence` / `chore: seal change evidence` maps the dogfood loop writes for itself, each citing one span for every hunk; 45 maps have negative specificity (umbrella citations that a cyclic shift of the hunk order matches as well as the real plan) and 17 maps have evidence fan-out >= 100. Cause: `make dogfood-change` takes a flat DOGFOOD_CITATIONS TSV (ORDINAL, path, lines, class) and the bind/seal rounds reuse one spec span for every hunk, so the producer writes maps that the cem/1.0 consumer-computed tiers grade as cited/invariant by construction. Expected after the decision 0525 cutover (V1-1276): the producer emits one citation per hunk from the change's own evidence (spec section, test, decision) and the self-referential bind/seal maps are recognised as their own class so they do not dominate every tier metric. Actual: a careful change and a rubber-stamp change look the same at the producer, which is the exact failure cem/1.0 exists to expose. Scope: producer and dogfood loop only; the consumer tiers (CEM-V1-080..082) do not change.
title: dogfood producer: per-hunk citations and a distinct class for self-referential bind/seal maps
